arxiv-2007-03545.title: Network Embedding with Completely-imbalanced Labels
arxiv-2007-03545.creator: Zheng Wang, Xiaojun Ye, Chaokun Wang, Jian Cui, Philip S. Yu
arxiv-2007-03545.description: Abstract Network embedding, aiming to project a network into a low-dimensional space, is increasingly becoming a focus of network research. Semi-supervised network embedding takes advantage of labeled data, and has shown promising performance. However, existing semi-supervised methods would get unappealing results in the completely-imbalanced label setting where some classes have no labeled nodes at all.

arxiv-2203-11580.title: The second cohomology of regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties from GKM theory
arxiv-2203-11580.creator: Anton Ayzenberg, Mikiya Masuda, Takashi Sato
arxiv-2203-11580.description: Abstract . We describe the second cohomology of a regular semisimple Hessenberg variety by generators and relations explicitly in terms of GKM theory. The cohomology of a regular semisimple Hessenberg variety becomes a module of a symmetric group 𝔖 n \mathfrak{S}_{n} by the dot action introduced by Tymoczko.

arxiv-2209-08243.title: DiPietro-Hazari Kappa: A Novel Metric for Assessing Labeling Quality via Annotation
arxiv-2209-08243.creator: Daniel M. DiPietro*, Vivek Hazari*
arxiv-2209-08243.description: Abstract Data is a key component of modern machine learning, but statistics for assessing data label quality remain sparse in literature. Here, we introduce DiPietro-Hazari Kappa, a novel statistical metric for assessing the quality of suggested dataset labels in the context of human annotation.

arxiv-2212-08386.title: Rheology of dilute granular gas mixtures where the grains interact via a square shoulder and well potential
arxiv-2212-08386.creator: Kiwamu Yoshii, Satoshi Takada, Kosuke Kurosawa, Thorsten Pöschel
arxiv-2212-08386.description: Abstract We develop the rheology of a dilute granular gas mixture. Motivated by the interaction of charged granular particles, we assume that the grains interact via a square shoulder and well potential. Employing kinetic theory, we compute the temperature and the shear viscosity as functions of the shear rate. Numerical simulations confirm our results above the critical shear rate.

arxiv-2301-09717.creator: Qingchao Li, Mohammed El-Hajjar, Senior Member, IEEE, Ibrahim Hemadeh, Member, IEEE, Arman Shojaeifard, Senior Member, IEEE, Alain A. M. Mourad, Lajos Hanzo, Life Fellow, IEEE

arxiv-2311-08238.title: Images of dominant endomorphisms of affine space
arxiv-2311-08238.creator: Viktor Balch Barth, Tuyen Trung Truong
arxiv-2311-08238.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Viktor Balch Barth, Tuyen Trung Truong. A basic problem in the study of algebraic morphisms is to determine which sets can be realised as the image of an endomorphism of affine space. This paper extends the results previously obtained by the first author on the question of existence of surjective maps F : 𝔸 n → 𝔸 n ∖ Z F\colon\mathbb{A}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{n}\setminus Z , where Z Z is an algebraic subvariety of 𝔸 n \mathbb{A}^{n} of codimension at least 2.

arxiv-2507-17484.title: A standard clt for triangles in a class of ergs
arxiv-2507-17484.creator: Elena Magnanini, Giacomo Passuello
arxiv-2507-17484.description: Abstract We prove a standard Central Limit Theorem for the (normalized) number of triangles in a class of Exponential Random Graphs derived from a slight modification of the edge-triangle model. Our main theorem covers the whole analyticity region of the free energy, and is based on a polynomial representation of the partition function.

pmc-10485940.title: Life expectancy and healthy life expectancy of Korean registered disabled by disability type in 2014–2018: Korea National Rehabilitation Center database
pmc-10485940.creator: Hyuna Jang, Kyung-Hwa Choi, Jung-Ae Kim, Yong-jun Choi
pmc-10485940.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundConducting a distinct comparison between the life expectancy (LE) and healthy life expectancy (HALE) of people with disabilities (PWDs) and the general population is necessary due to the various environmental and health conditions they encounter. Therefore, this study aimed to develop the life table for PWDs and calculate those of LE and HALE based on sex, severity, and disability types among the registered Korean PWDs.MethodsWe used aggregated data of registered PWDs from the Korea National Rehabilitation Center database between 2014 and 2018.

pmc-11385801.title: The influence of geographical location on moisture distribution in wood cross sections: a numerical simulation study using Austria as an example
pmc-11385801.creator: Florian Brandstätter, Maximilian Autengruber, Markus Lukacevic, Josef Füssl
pmc-11385801.description: Wood constantly interacts with the surrounding, locally varying climate, leading to changes in the moisture content. Advanced simulation tools can predict the two-dimensional moisture distributions caused by these changing climate conditions within wood cross sections over time. However, there is a notable absence of systematic simulation results for diverse climatic conditions and various wood cross sections.

pmc-11509788.title: Factors Influencing the Clinical Course of Bullous Pemphigoid among Geriatric Patients: A Pilot Study
pmc-11509788.creator: Paula Mazan, Aleksandra Lesiak, Igor Bednarski, Dorota Sobolewska-Sztychny, Marcin Noweta, Joanna Narbutt, Mauro Salvatore Alessandro Alaibac
pmc-11509788.description: Background and Objectives: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is the most common autoimmune blistering disease affecting mainly elderly patients. Still, little is known about the pathogenesis of pruritus in BP or the factors that affect the clinical course of the disease. This study aimed to evaluate the factors influencing the clinical course of BP among older patients.

pmc-11677133.title: Australians’ Well-Being and Resilience During COVID-19: The Role of Trust, Misinformation, Intolerance of Uncertainty, and Locus of Control
pmc-11677133.creator: Nida Denson, Kevin M Dunn, Alanna Kamp, Jehonathan Ben, Daniel Pitman, Rachel Sharples, Grace Lim, Yin Paradies, Craig McGarty, Michele Roccella, Gennaro Ruggiero, Valeria Carola, Giampaolo Nicolais
pmc-11677133.description: Background/Objectives: In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, Australian state and federal governments enacted boarder closures, social distancing measures, and lockdowns. By the end of October 2020, the 112-day lockdown in the Australian state of Victoria was the longest continuous lockdown period internationally.

pmc-12597667.title: Between sound and sleep: a perspective on Sonic Sleep Aids
pmc-12597667.creator: Jessica Vazzaz, Faith Matcham, Marcos Economides, Kate Cavanagh
pmc-12597667.description: Sleep disturbances are prevalent in the general population, coinciding with a surge in the availability and use of digital sleep aids. Among these, standalone audio-based tools, termed Sonic Sleep Aids (SSA), such as sleep music, ambient sounds, bedtime stories, and sleep skills (e.g. guided meditation, positive psychology techniques), have gained popularity.

pmc-13052860.title: Dissecting executive dysfunction in children: The role of psychosocial disabilities through Bayesian and ANOVA approaches
pmc-13052860.creator: Soo Eun Chae
pmc-13052860.description: This study investigates the relationship between executive dysfunction and psychosocial disabilities in children aged 8–11, utilizing data from the Korean Child Panel Study collected between 2015 and 2018. The dataset, consisting of 1,196 valid responses, was analyzed using a Latent Growth Model, which revealed that a quadratic model best fit the data.

pmc-13185207.title: From Precision to Personalized: Catalyzing AI‐Enabled Innovation in Drug Development
pmc-13185207.creator: Adarsh Subbaswamy, Allison Dunn, Brooke Langevin, Sooyoung Lee, Mathangi Gopalakrishnan, Jogarao V S Gobburu
pmc-13185207.description: In 2015, President Obama announced the Precision Medicine Initiative in his nationally televised State of the Union address. The vision was bold: to enable a new era of medicine through research, technology, and policies that empower patients, researchers, and providers to work together toward the development of individualized care.

pmc-13188121.title: High-grade glioma with dural progression: A single-center case series and review of literature
pmc-13188121.creator: George Wang, Abraham Nirappel, Arashdeep Kaur, Douglas Martin, Prashant Vempati, Tiffany Hodges, Chaitra Badve
pmc-13188121.description: Glioblastoma is the most common and aggressive primary brain tumor in adults. However, despite its aggressive nature, dural-based progression remains exceedingly rare. This rarity is partially due to the protective effects of the blood-brain barrier and the poor survival of affected patients. As a result, the pathophysiology and imaging characteristics of dural-based glioblastoma progression remain poorly understood and underreported.

pmc-13336311.title: Upadacitinib in Biologic-Naïve Patients With Acute Severe Ulcerative Colitis: A Case Report of a Promising Alternative Rescue Therapy
pmc-13336311.creator: Sneh Parekh, Antoine Boustany, Yasasvhinie Santharam, Claudia Aleman Oliva, Camille Lupianez, Andrew T Flint, Scott Smith, Marianny Sulbaran
pmc-13336311.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Acute severe ulcerative colitis (ASUC) is a known complication of ulcerative colitis (UC). Treatment of ASUC is with intravenous (IV) corticosteroids as first-line therapy and with infliximab or cyclosporine as rescue therapy in disease refractory to steroids. Upadacitinib is a newer and alternative therapy for patients, particularly after they have received at least one approved systemic therapy, if tumor necrosis factor (TNF) blockers are clinically inadvisable.

pmc-13477348.title: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Control Among Young Adults With Diabetes in the United States Between 2013 and 2023
pmc-13477348.creator: Alexander R Zheutlin, Joshua A Jacobs, Alexander Chaitoff
pmc-13477348.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). s nearly 5% to 10% of US adults with diabetes and has risen annually for 2 decades, making cardiovascular risk factor control a defining priority for this population. 1 , 2 , 3 We examined secular trends in cardiovascular disease risk factor control for young adults with diabetes (type 1 or type 2) between 2013 and 2023 to characterize this cardiovascular care gap. All data used are publicly available via the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

pmc-13546808.title: Integrating rare and common variation in epilepsy genetics: from genetic architecture to penetrance and clinical expressivity
pmc-13546808.creator: Ming-Shan Cai, Hou-Rui Li, Peng Liao, Zhen-Liang Hu, Yong-Jun Chen
pmc-13546808.description: Epilepsy genetics has often been interpreted through a useful but simplified dichotomous framework in which severe epilepsies, particularly developmental and epileptic encephalopathies, are attributed mainly to rare, high-effect variants, whereas more common epilepsies are viewed as arising largely from the cumulative effects of common, small-effect variation.
